title: Before the prayer
hook: conditions: being Muslim, sane, of age, clean, covered, facing the qiblah, in time

segments.voice: Yesterday, last words, and your line: let these be my last words. What was the last thing you said before sleep? Today a new part opens: the prayer. Day one thousand seventy-three.

Gate 23, a delayed flight, and the afternoon prayer time already open. A woman sets down her bag and runs a quiet checklist. Did her wudu survive the security line? She thinks it did. Is her scarf where it should be? Yes. Is the carpet by the window clean enough? She lays a jacket down to be sure. Which way is Mecca from here? Her phone's compass points past the vending machine. How long until the time runs out? Long enough. Only then does she raise her hands and say Allahu akbar. Everything before that moment has a name.
screen: `A DELAYED FLIGHT, AN OPEN PRAYER TIME.` → `A QUIET CHECKLIST.` → `ONLY THEN: ALLAHU AKBAR.`

segments.voice: The name is shurut, conditions. In the fiqh books, the conditions are the things that must already be true before the prayer starts, before that opening Allahu akbar, the takbir. They sit outside the prayer, like the frame around a door. The parts inside the prayer, the standing, bowing and prostrating, have a different name, and they come later. Start with the person. The prayer is the act of a Muslim, who is of sound mind and has reached the age of responsibility. A hadith in Sunan Abu Dawud, number 4403, says the pen is lifted from three: the sleeper until he wakes, the child until he grows up, and the one who has lost his reason until he recovers. The duty itself waits for that. Then the body and the place. Clean: Sahih Muslim, number 224, says a prayer is not accepted without purification. Covered: the Qur'an, in Pickthall's translation, says, "O Children of Adam! Look to your adornment at every place of worship." The schools spell out what covering means, and they differ in the details. Then direction. The Qur'an tells the Prophet ﷺ, "So turn thy face toward the Inviolable Place of Worship," the Ka'ba in Mecca. Then time. The Qur'an says that "worship at fixed hours hath been enjoined on the believers." A prayer said before its time has opened hasn't yet met its condition. Read the list again and it's almost all about arriving: arrive in the right state, at the right moment, facing the right way. The prayer itself can then be about only one thing.
screen: `CONDITIONS: TRUE BEFORE IT STARTS.` · `THE PERSON: MUSLIM, SANE, OF AGE.` · `CLEAN, COVERED, FACING THE KA'BA.` · `IN ITS TIME.` · then, large: `WORSHIP AT FIXED HOURS.`

segments.voice: The practice: check each one, slowly, the way the woman at the gate did. Settle where you are. First, the body: notice your hands, your face, whether you feel clean. Then your clothes: are you dressed the way you'd want to be before something that matters? Then direction: which way are you facing right now, and do you know where Mecca lies from here? Then time: what part of the day is this? If you pray, you can do this check before your next prayer. If you don't, use it before your next important conversation. The bell holds the time.
Shurut. Conditions: what must already be true before the prayer begins. The person, clean, covered, facing the qiblah, and in time. Today's word.

Your line: ready before the takbir. Today, before one thing you start, a meal, a call, a prayer, take five seconds to check that you've arrived. Tomorrow, wudu in detail. Day one thousand seventy-three.

howItsDone: Before each prayer, Muslims make sure they are in a state of purification, dressed with the required covering, on a clean spot, facing the Ka'ba in Mecca, and within the prayer's time, and only then begin with Allahu akbar.
